naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under, such as `wells`. A blank value counts as none.
Optional text describing the cache.

The document kind: `cache`, a cache flow that fills a partition's cache with the reference data mappings resolve against. The loader chooses the reader by it and refuses a document that declares no `flowType` or `documentType`.

Removed. Every version a refresh writes becomes the current version of its partition's cache, so a cache flow that still declares `makeCurrent` is refused when it loads. A delivery flow that has to stay on an earlier version pins it with `render.cacheVersion`.

The cache flow's name: its pipeline identity, and the name the versions it writes and the records it holds in the partition's cache are recorded under. A cache flow is named globally: the sync warns when a second file, in this repository or another, declares the same name.

What a changed cached value does to the records already built from it. `auto` tags them and lets the next run carry the new document; `approve` tags them and holds them back until someone approves the update on the OSDU cache page. A type can override it with `types[].onChange`.

Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in a type's `query`; a token no parameter declares is refused. Values come from `--set name=value`, the run's values, or the schedule's `values`.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.
The value used when a run supplies none.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.
The HTTP settings for the platform's searches, as on a delivery flow: timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size. `reliability.parallelInterfaces` is refused.
A delivery flow's setting: rendered documents per work batch file. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: records claimed per ledger round trip when retrying records. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: how many record batches its worker sends at once. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the member runs a large submission spreads over. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: below this many records a submission never fans out. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.
A delivery source's setting: how many of its interfaces run at once. A cache flow runs no interfaces, so the loader refuses it here.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.
A delivery flow's setting: renderers in the intake pipeline (0 = the machine's cores). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a cache flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.

Where the flow reads from: the OSDU platform its OSDU types are searched on (`endpoint`, `auth`, `headers`) and the ingestion database its table types are read from (`connection`). `source.headers` names the partition whose cache the flow fills, so the block is always required.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Only with `source.endpoint`, when a type declares `kind`; refused when every type is a table or dictionary type.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is basic or oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one).
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is bearer or apiKeyHeader.

keys.description: The ingestion database the flow's table types are read from, declared as a delivery flow's `source.connection` is: a whole ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret} reference, or a SQL Server connection string whose secrets are references. A literal password is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: Required when a type declares `table`; refused when none does.

keys.description: The base URL of the OSDU platform the OSDU types are searched on, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`. The cache flows of one partition should search the same platform: the sync warns when they declare different endpoints.
keys.appliesWhen: Required when a type declares `kind`; refused, with `source.auth`, when every type is a table or dictionary type.

keys.description: Headers sent with every request to the platform. `data-partition-id` is always required: it names the partition whose cache the flow fills, and every search carries it.

One header; `<name>` is the header name. `data-partition-id` is an id segment (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and dot, at most 200 characters) or a `${env:...}` or `${keyvault:...}` reference; a cache is keyed by what it resolves to.

The types the flow caches, at least one. Each has exactly one origin: `kind` (searched on OSDU), `table` (an ingestion table) or `dictionary` (a dictionary document in the repository). Type names are unique within the flow, because a mapping reads a type by its name (`cache.<Type>.<field>`).

One cached type. Another cache flow of the same partition may declare the same OSDU type, and the cache then holds one type under that name; a lookup table (a table or dictionary type) is declared by one cache flow of a partition.

The name of the dictionary document the type holds: `dictionaries/<name>.yaml` in the nearest `dictionaries/` folder above the flow. The type is named after the dictionary unless `name` says otherwise, is kept as `lookup--<name>`, and takes no `kind`, `entityType`, `query` or `fields`, since the document names its key and values. The run reads the file at its commit, so it needs the repository's tree.
keys.appliesWhen: Dictionary origin only: a type with `dictionary`, held from the repository's dictionaries/ folder. Not combined with `kind` or `table`.

keys.description: The OSDU entity type of the records (`reference-data--UnitOfMeasure`). Derived from the kind when left out; a kind that names no entity type needs it.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU origin only: a type with `kind`, searched on OSDU. Refused on a table or dictionary type.

keys.description: What the cache keeps of each record. For an OSDU type: the paths to keep. For a table type: the columns to keep beside the key. A path that yields nothing on every record is reported at capture.
keys.appliesWhen: Required for an OSDU type (`kind`) and a table type (`table`); refused for a dictionary type (`dictionary`).

keys.description: One kept value. For an OSDU type: a path such as `data.Code` (cached as `Code`), or `{ path: ..., as: ... }`. For a table type: a column name (kept under its own name), or `{ column: ..., as: ... }`. Whatever a path yields is cached as it is: a scalar, a set of values, or a nested object.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU and table origins; a dictionary type lists none.

keys.description: The path into the OSDU record, from its root (`data.Code`, `legal.legaltags`). A path crosses arrays implicitly, so `data.NameAliases.AliasName` reaches through an array of objects and caches the set of aliases it finds.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU origin only: a type with `kind`, searched on OSDU. Required in the `{ path: ..., as: ... }` form.

keys.description: The name the value is kept under, and the name a mapping reads it by. For an OSDU type a bare path is kept under the path without its leading `data.`; the name `id` is refused, and no two values of a type share a name. For a table type a column is kept under its own name; neither the key nor a field may be called `id` in any casing.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU origin (with `path`) or table origin (with `column`).

keys.description: A column of the table to keep beside the key: 1 to 128 characters, without brackets, control characters or surrounding space. The key column is not listed among the fields, since it is kept under its own name already.
keys.appliesWhen: Table origin only: a type with `table`, read from an ingestion table. Required in the `{ column: ..., as: ... }` form.

keys.description: The column each row of the table is keyed by, and the one a mapping finds the row by. A key is trimmed, and a key that is empty, longer than 256 characters, or held by two rows once trimmed refuses the capture, naming the rows.
keys.appliesWhen: Table origin only: a type with `table`, read from an ingestion table. Required there; refused on an OSDU type, whose records are kept under their id, and on a dictionary type, whose document names its own key.

keys.description: The OSDU kind searched, `authority:source:entityType:version` with wildcards per segment (`osdu:wks:reference-data--UnitOfMeasure:*`). A refresh sweeps every record the search matches through the search cursor.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU origin only: a type with `kind`, searched on OSDU. Not combined with `table` or `dictionary`; it makes `source.endpoint` required.

keys.description: The name a mapping reads the type by (`cache.<Type>.<field>`), unique within the flow ignoring case. Derived when left out: from the entity type for an OSDU type (`reference-data--UnitOfMeasure` gives `UnitOfMeasure`), from the table name for a table type, and from the dictionary name for a dictionary type.

Overrides the flow's `onChange` for this type: `auto` lets the next run carry a changed value, `approve` holds the affected records until someone approves the update on the OSDU cache page. When several cache flows of a partition declare a type, its changes wait for approval when any of them says `approve`.
A Lucene query narrowing the records the type's search matches. `{name}` tokens are substituted from the flow's parameters; a token no parameter declares is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: OSDU origin only: a type with `kind`, searched on OSDU. Refused on a table or dictionary type, which holds every row.

keys.description: The three-part name (`[database].[schema].[table]`) of an ingestion table an ingestion flow loads, read over `source.connection`. The type is named after the table unless `name` says otherwise, is kept as `lookup--<name>`, and holds every row its ingestion flow has not marked deleted (`DeletedDate_DW`, when the table has it); a table over 100,000 rows refuses the capture. Lineage orders the flow after the ingestion flow that loads the table.
keys.appliesWhen: Table origin only: a type with `table`, read from an ingestion table. Not combined with `kind` or `dictionary`; needs `key` and `fields`, and makes `source.connection` required.
